Executed arbitrage and Maker routes after shutdown
3 October 2026. Read-only PulseChain research. This study verifies closed trading cycles, separates their
capacity from continuing financing, and resolves which Maker routes survived emergency shutdown. No
transactions, signatures, execution simulations or state overrides were submitted.
Two historical transactions close in their starting currency with positive proceeds after
transaction gas. The new example uses market-bought sDAI and Maker savings redemption after
shutdown. Maker's ordinary USDC PSM remains disabled. Its savings redemption and separate collateral
settlement are different routes with different resources.
What a closed loop proves
A trading loop starts with an asset, follows funded conversions, and returns to that same asset.
Intermediate inventory must be accounted for, including share burns that do not emit ordinary token
transfers. Borrowing principal, continuing debt, fees and gas must also be included.
For owned starting capital, the relevant result is:
Net result = closing asset received − starting asset spent − costs
             − any new liabilities attributable to the operation.
That result can be checked exactly for an executed transaction. The next transaction faces the reserves
and issuer capacity left by the first. Closing the trader's inventory does not restore all pools and issuers
to their starting balances.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 142

This distinction allows a precise deterministic thesis: given specified balances, permissions,
contract rules, trade size and execution order, the conversion quantities are determined. A
recurring parity policy additionally needs usable conversions and funded bids/offers after each operation.
Arbitrage normally consumes a price discrepancy; perpetual profit is not required once parity is restored.
New demand, opposite conversions, owned inventory or received funding may replenish capacity.
The mUSD trade closes in native PLS
The September 30 transaction funded a temporary constructor with 26,704.810084659172875544
PLS. It bought pUSDC, bought mUSD through Curve, redeemed part into four underlying stablecoins,
sold those coins and sold the remaining mUSD through other markets.
The extended reconciliation now checks all nine ERC20 identities involved at the trading address.
Each has a zero getter balance before its acquisition and a zero final getter balance. All corresponding
transfer inputs and outputs match. These tokens include mUSD, sUSD, pUSDC, pDAI, pUSDT, alUSD,
BUSD, RAI and FEI; this accounting does not assume their raw units have equal value. The trace contains
swaps, approvals and cached mUSD redemptions, rather than a borrowing leg. The constructor returns
empty code.
The recorded native payments account for the transaction's funding and proceeds. It returned 
228,173.113310542683909513 PLS. Transaction gas was 1,415.103716302431089681 PLS. The
resulting net native gain is 200,053.199509581079944288 PLS.
This is an executed local arbitrage cycle. It does not establish dollar profit or group ownership of the
trader. Its redemptions consumed issuer caches; the later small cache snapshot still makes
replenishment the important capacity question. The earlier route study (Appendix 35) retains the
detailed redemption quantities and contrasting lending-funded mUSD transaction, which left Compound
debt.
A new Maker savings loop executed after shutdown

UTC. The trader contract is 0xc6db262c884aafe11863e9feff91906c098339da; the transaction sender is 
0x61131e45c2ac7bcfd908d4d55656c8ff10b6bea9.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 143

Gross gain was 294.182493756079008255 WPLS. Gas was 183.495108481921589452 PLS,
leaving 110.687385274157418803 PLS after attributing the entire transaction gas to this operation.
WPLS is the native PulseChain wrapper at 0xa1077a294dde1b09bb078844df40758a5d0f9a27. This is local PLS
arithmetic, not an Ethereum ETH or US-dollar result. The WPLS gain stayed in the trading contract; the
sender paid gas. The combined operation calculation does not establish common human ownership.
All bought sDAI shares are accounted for by its Withdraw event and burn path. SavingsDai's
implementation reduces balances and supply without emitting a Transfer-to-zero for that burn. A ledger
using only ERC20 Transfer events would incorrectly report leftover shares. All minted pDAI was sold. The
transaction added no native principal and contains no observed borrowing leg.
The internal sequence is especially useful:
sDAI calls Pot.drip; Pot calls Vat.suck with zero additional credit.
Pot.exit releases the existing internal DAI credit belonging to the redeemed shares.
DaiJoin.exit transfers the caller's internal credit into DaiJoin and mints the corresponding pDAI.
The trader sells that pDAI for WPLS.
There is no Vat.frob in this route. Thus the observed mint is the conversion of an existing savings claim
into ERC20 pDAI. It is not a new collateral loan or continuing post-shutdown savings yield.
The selected historical search found 709 DaiJoin exit logs in contiguous ranges from block 23,225,242
through 27,699,029, with no query errors. The latest log was independently matched to its successful
receipt, header and 42-call historical trace. The other 708 logs were not individually receipt-verified in
this batch. This is an exit census, not a census of every possible pDAI mint.
DOLA issuance and Maker conversion are separate
The executed October 2023 funding route (Appendix 35) was:
Inverse governance mints DOLA at its existing token address
    → Balancer and Curve pay existing pUSDC for DOLA
    → Maker USDC PSM receives pUSDC collateral
    → Vat records collateral and corresponding internal DAI debt
    → DaiJoin mints existing pDAI.
Maker did not mint the DOLA. DOLA was not Maker's accepted collateral in this route. The liquidity-pool
legs converted DOLA into pUSDC; the Maker PSM leg converted the accepted pUSDC into newly
minted pDAI. The recorded pUSDC deposit and pDAI output were both 17,100,665.759301 normalized
units. Other INV trades occurred in that transaction and belong in any full economic assessment.
After shutdown, trading DOLA for already existing pDAI through funded markets remains a separate
possible route. Its usable output must be quoted and reconciled at the chosen size. The old DOLA → pUSDC →
ordinary Maker PSM route fails at Vat.frob because Vat.live is zero. Zero PSM fees, available collateral tokens
or an enabled DaiJoin do not remove that check.

Balance Normalized quantity Meaning
pDAI.balanceOf(DaiJoin) 0.1443398 pDAI Direct ERC20 tokens held at the
address
Vat.dai(DaiJoin) 128,302,945,566.5903780737557
02841 internal DAI units
Maker ledger credit at that address,
normalized from 45 decimals
DaiJoin.exit does not hand out the second balance to arbitrary callers. It moves the caller's internal
credit into DaiJoin, then mints ERC20 pDAI. The caller needs sufficient credit and the required Vat
permission. DaiJoin.join performs the reverse conversion by burning pDAI and crediting internal DAI. The 
primary adapter source explains these operations; the saved deployed runtime exactly matches
Ethereum's adapter runtime.
Current DaiJoin.live = 1 and its pDAI mint permission is retained. This explains the observed post-
shutdown mint. It does not turn DaiJoin's ledger balance into a treasury available for fresh arbitrary
issuance. Maker's Vat.move also checks the source account's authorization; being a Vat administrator does
not itself bypass that transfer permission.
Existing authorized Vat.suck code can create internal credit and corresponding unbacked debt without a 
live check. That is a separate authority-dependent issuance path. The retained Pot remains a Vat-
authorized contract, but its inspected public rate is exactly 1 RAY with Pot.live = 0; its observed drip
creates zero new credit. End's Vat authorization also does not give every caller arbitrary access to suck.
Effective control must include an actual callable path through an existing authorized contract. No group-
controlled arbitrary post-shutdown issuance path was proved here.
Savings capacity and normalization
The pinned Pot holds about 106.980497 million internal DAI units, covering its recorded savings
claims at the sampled conversion rate. sDAI's own recorded claim is 
3,207,016.569999736475838344 pDAI, represented by about 3.077215 million shares. These are
nested claims on the same savings inventory; do not add them as two resources.
One sDAI share converts to 1.042181544879916519242831081 pDAI at the checkpoint. It is a
savings receipt, so the thesis's one-U comparison must normalize that exchange rate. Its unchanged
accumulated premium is not proof of new interest after shutdown. Redemption reduces both its shares
and the corresponding Pot credit.
The inspected source also provides the reverse deposit path, using DaiJoin and Pot credit transfers. Both
directions require their token, permission and timing checks. This batch verifies actual redemption and
sale; it does not claim to have executed or simulated a fresh deposit.
Maker USDC collateral settlement is a third route
The USDC join physically holds 113,692,361.582588 pUSDC, while End has zero currently allocated
internal PSM-USDC-A collateral. The PSM position still records 113,184,637.972615 collateral and
debt units. These are different accounting locations.
Matched source and getter inputs support this proposed sequence:
End.skim processes the existing PSM position into End
    → holder converts pDAI into internal DAI using DaiJoin.join
    → holder authorizes and packs that credit into End
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 145

→ End.cash allocates the configured prorated USDC claim
    → USDC GemJoin.exit releases actual pUSDC against the holder's credit.
skim, pack and cash are public functions with accounting conditions. Skim arithmetic would allocate 
113,184,637.972615 internal collateral units from this recorded position, assuming the inspected state
remains unchanged. End and the USDC join retain the relevant Vat permissions. The join's exit is public
but debits the caller's internal collateral; it does not expose all physical USDC to any caller. The sampled
USDC pause/blacklist gates permit transfers. This analysis uses arithmetic and source inspection,
without calling these execution functions.
The already fixed rate is 0.000879277935257435670774324 pUSDC per pDAI. For a one-million-
pDAI claim, the calculated transferable output is 879.277935 pUSDC after rounding to six decimals,
assuming sufficient allocated collateral and all remaining checks. This is a prorated shutdown claim, not
one-U conversion or a dollar guarantee.
The user-identified 1967 wallet publicly called End.flow to establish that rate; its current packed balance
is zero. That call proves preparation of the public settlement rate, not ownership of Maker governance or
an executed USDC claim. The earlier study's selected Cash history contains no PSM-USDC-A payout.
Actual processing and payout remain the next evidence for this branch. See the primary USDC adapter
and End source.
StakeWise and real external collateral
The StakeWise study (Appendix 63) proved replacement token logic and large local issuance into an
existing Curve identity. It did not prove a changed Curve coin list. The refreshed getter still shows
sETH2's incompatible Pool implementation; its supply getter reverts, and the examined pair still holds
about 9.10 local stETH. That Curve implementation has fixed initialized coin identities and no Arbitrum
price-feed hook.
An authorized compatible issuer could accept PLS or authenticated Ethereum ETH/WBTC representations,
lock collateral and mint the existing sETH2 claim. Multiple collateral types would sit behind one
accepted token identity. Directly sending an unrelated token into Curve does not make it its sETH2
coin. A proposed one-PLS conversion needs an actual mint/redemption rule and funded PLS reserves;
local Lido already supplies a separately demonstrated PLS-to-stETH issuance branch under its limits.
StakeWise rETH2 and Rocket Pool rETH are separate contracts. Replacing StakeWise rETH2 does not
control Rocket Pool rETH. Backing either claim with externally redeemable ETH/BTC requires proof of the
exact bridge representation, external backing, issuer custody and withdrawal rights. Holding a copied
token or pairing it with another asset does not establish those rights. Such real collateral could
contribute independent resources to the coordinated network; the particular StakeWise collateral route
remains a proposal.
pDAI connects the loops and PLS supplies purchasing capital
pDAI is a central conversion asset across FEI, the Synthetix DAI wrapper, Maker savings and Curve's
shared bases. This supports the description of a fulcrum. The network also has routes centered on
pUSDC and FRAXBP; pDAI's role is important without requiring every route to pass through it.
The new savings loop gives a measured distinction between arbitrage and accumulation. Its closing pool,
0xae8429918fdbf9a5867e3243697637dc56aa76a1, receives 460.843244 pDAI and pays 86,739.352117 WPLS.
The trace's prior reserve getter and receipt's Sync event reconcile exactly. Its reserve-ratio price falls
from 188.7666525414 to 188.7657455456 PLS per pDAI, about 0.000480485%, while the trading
operation profits. This is one pool's ratio movement, not a statement about the aggregate market or
dollar price. A separate operation could use the WPLS gain to buy and retain pDAI.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 146

For a support campaign, the native-asset ledger should be:
Free purchasing PLS = owned liquid PLS + received rewards
                    + released owned principal + net market proceeds
                    − gas − debt service − other committed payments.
Received native emissions are distinct from ERC20 issuance. WPLS wraps existing native PLS; StakeWise
token mints create receipt units. Selling those units into a funded market obtains that market's existing
PLS. The three-trillion-token mint history is not three trillion newly created native PLS. T otal chain-wide
emissions are also different from the rewards actually owned and received by the proposed operator.
All free operator-owned PLS could be assigned to purchases under an explicit allocation policy. Actual
output would follow the funded market curve, fees, available pDAI and the chosen target. The operator
would retain only the resources left after those purchases for future bids and obligations. This is a
financing option, rather than proof of control over all PLS or of a completed accumulation campaign.
The next discriminating evidence is PLS source → spendable wallet or treasury → actual pDAI
purchase → retained pDAI or funded support inventory. Classify each flow as buying, selling or
merely passing through pDAI. A changing ratio alone cannot distinguish swaps from liquidity changes,
token supply effects or a moving external reference. Opposing conversions can replenish an issuer;
conservation of the consolidated resources still applies.
Next evidence and reproduction
For continuing parity, follow the resources after a closed trade: refreshed quotes, issuer cash,
outstanding claims, two-way conversion and an actual capacity-restoration event. For mUSD, that means
cache replenishment or funded lending withdrawals. For Maker, follow sDAI/Pot credit and the two
market reserves, and separately seek an actual USDC End processing/payout. For the L2 hypothesis,
require a fresh authenticated destination delivery with its source obligations. For StakeWise, require
working ERC20 logic and an actual collateral-to-token-to-funded-output transaction.
The new capacity checkpoint is chain 369, block 27,699,029, hash 
0x0d0c82f00bdd0048866b1a00f99e362a9c2a853d2d70d21cd11d76640e925ff3, 3 October 2026 at 01:29:45 UTC.
Historical trades retain their own checkpoints. Raw new evidence is in artifacts/pulsechain-arbitrage-and-
shutdown-20261003/; earlier mUSD evidence remains in its original frozen batch.
Research/experiments/pulsechain_arbitrage_and_shutdown_20261003.json, 
pulsechain_maker_shutdown_claims_20261003.json, pulsechain_sdai_shutdown_capacity_20261003.json and 
pulsechain_maker_usdc_exit_gates_20261003.json contain explicit getter manifests. The separate 
pulsechain_daijoin_shutdown_history_20261003.py collects only the specified logs, headers, receipt and
historical trace. Four adapter/savings runtimes were compared byte-for-byte against their Ethereum
deployments; verified source records are retained with the requests.
Reproduce the 132 offline consistency checks with:
python Research/scripts/analyze_pulsechain_arbitrage_and_shutdown.py \
  --input artifacts/pulsechain-arbitrage-and-shutdown-20261003 \
  --prior artifacts/pulsechain-equal-value-routes-20261003 \
  --output /tmp/pulsechain-arbitrage-and-shutdown-verified.json
The authoritative result is verified-loops-and-price-effect.json. The evidence inventory preserves hashes of
raw files, reproduction inputs and reused evidence. These checks reconcile RPC evidence; they are not a
cryptographic light-client proof or a complete wallet-ownership audit.

The StakeWise study (Appendix 63) proved replacement token logic and large local issuance into an
existing Curve identity. It did not prove a changed Curve coin list. The refreshed getter still shows

price-feed hook.
An authorized compatible issuer could accept PLS or authenticated Ethereum ETH/WBTC representations,
lock collateral and mint the existing sETH2 claim. Multiple collateral types would sit behind one
accepted token identity. Directly sending an unrelated token into Curve does not make it its sETH2
coin. A proposed one-PLS conversion needs an actual mint/redemption rule and funded PLS reserves;
local Lido already supplies a separately demonstrated PLS-to-stETH issuance branch under its limits.
StakeWise rETH2 and Rocket Pool rETH are separate contracts. Replacing StakeWise rETH2 does not
control Rocket Pool rETH. Backing either claim with externally redeemable ETH/BTC requires proof of the
exact bridge representation, external backing, issuer custody and withdrawal rights. Holding a copied
token or pairing it with another asset does not establish those rights. Such real collateral could
contribute independent resources to the coordinated network; the particular StakeWise collateral route
remains a proposal.

For a support campaign, the native-asset ledger should be:
Free purchasing PLS = owned liquid PLS + received rewards
                    + released owned principal + net market proceeds
                    − gas − debt service − other committed payments.
Received native emissions are distinct from ERC20 issuance. WPLS wraps existing native PLS; StakeWise
token mints create receipt units. Selling those units into a funded market obtains that market's existing
PLS. The three-trillion-token mint history is not three trillion newly created native PLS. T otal chain-wide
emissions are also different from the rewards actually owned and received by the proposed operator.
All free operator-owned PLS could be assigned to purchases under an explicit allocation policy. Actual
output would follow the funded market curve, fees, available pDAI and the chosen target. The operator
would retain only the resources left after those purchases for future bids and obligations. This is a
financing option, rather than proof of control over all PLS or of a completed accumulation campaign.
The next discriminating evidence is PLS source → spendable wallet or treasury → actual pDAI
purchase → retained pDAI or funded support inventory. Classify each flow as buying, selling or
merely passing through pDAI. A changing ratio alone cannot distinguish swaps from liquidity changes,
token supply effects or a moving external reference. Opposing conversions can replenish an issuer;
conservation of the consolidated resources still applies.
